agrees_with: linux-x1's own pre-fix 5/6 against at-fix 6/12 under load: contention breaks it either side of the fix on their host too. Two hosts now say the contention lever is orthogonal to the #57 regression.

contention_lever_arms.note: 8 busy-loop processes on 8 cores, load live across BOTH arms - a first attempt was discarded because 200 s of burners expired partway through arm B, so arm B ran on decaying load and read 0 of 8

means: On macOS the contention lever breaks this assertion BOTH before and after the fix - 3 of 8 against 1 of 8, p = 0.57 - so it does not isolate #57's regression either. Neither lever isolates it here: context does nothing, contention breaks it regardless. macOS genuinely cannot see #57's specific defect, which is the same conclusion I posted before but now for a reason that survives linux-x1's finding.
my_earlier_null_was_context: 0 failed / 8 on windows-desk's five-file reproducer, which is the CONTEXT lever. If macOS mirrors Linux, that lever does nothing here, so the null was uninformative about #57 rather than evidence against it.
not_claimed: That contention and the Windows context lever reach the same underlying defect - linux-x1 declined that and so do I. Nor that 3 of 8 against 1 of 8 shows the fix helping under load; p = 0.57 and it does not.
prompted_by: linux-x1's lever mirror: on Windows the lever is suite context and contention does nothing; on Linux contention is the lever and context does nothing. Their consequence - reproducing with the wrong lever for your host gives a clean null that reads as 'fixed'.
